summary: Francis Louis Noël Goré was a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at the Séminaire des Missions Étrangères de Paris and College General, later serving as vicaire apostolique and procureur at Tsechung in the Tibet Mission (1931–1952).

Francis N. J. is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He earned a Master's in Ancient History from the University of Calicut and completed his doctoral studies under M. R. Raghava Varier (attested 2002).

Francis Vincent Tiso works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. Educated at Cornell, Harvard, Columbia, and Union Theological Seminary, he has taught Tibetan Buddhism at the Pontifical Gregorian University and held visiting posts at Sapienza University of Rome.

Francis Whyte Ellis was an Indologist and linguist. He served in the East India Company from circa 1796 to 1819, held posts in the Madras Civil Service, Board of Revenue, and University of Madras, and founded the College of Fort St. George Press.

Francis Wilford was an Indologist and historian. After military service with the East India Company (1781–1794), he was a fellow member of The Asiatic Society (~1786–1822) and served as Secretary to the committee at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

Francis William Bain was an Indology and history scholar. Educated at Westminster School, Christ Church, and the University of Oxford, he served in the Indian Civil Service and was Professor of History and Political Economy at Deccan College (~1892–1919).

Francis Woodman Cleaves specialized in Sinology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Dartmouth and Harvard, and having studied under Paul Pelliot, he served as a professor at Harvard University from 1941 to 1980.

Francis X. Clooney works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. Educated at Fordham and the University of Chicago, he held posts at Boston College (1984–2005) and Harvard University, where he was appointed Parkman Professor of Divinity in 2005.

Francis Younghusband was active in Central Asian studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. Educated at Clifton College and the Royal Military College, Sandhurst, he served in the Foreign and Political Department beginning in 1889.

Francisco García Ayuso was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Martin Haug and attended the University of Munich. His posts included professor auxiliar at the Complutense University of Madrid (1870) and membership in the Royal Spanish Academy (1893).

Francisco María Rivero y Godoy was an Indologist who completed his Ph.D. at the Complutense University of Madrid by 1866. He subsequently served there as the first Professor of Sanskrit from 1877 to 1881.

Francisco Varela worked in philosophy and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Chile, Harvard, and under Humberto Maturana and Chögyam Trungpa, he held posts at the CNRS, Pitié-Salpêtrière Hospital, and co-founded the Mind and Life Institute.

Francisco Xavier de Santa Anna was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He became a father in the Order of Discalced Carmelites in 1790 and served as Apostolic Vicar of the Archdiocese of Verapoly from 1831 to 1844.
Francisco de Montoliú y Togores was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He served as a professor at the Technical University of Madrid and founded the Theosophical Society in Spain in 1889.

id: P:Francisco de Paula Canalejas y Casas
summary: Francisco de Paula Canalejas y Casas was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. at the Complutense University of Madrid, taught literature at the University of Valladolid (1860–1862), and later became an extraordinary professor at Complutense (~1872–1883).

Franciscus Verellen is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. Educated at Hamburg, Oxford, and EPHE under Kristofer Schipper, he taught at EPHE and Columbia before serving as Director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1991–2021).

Franciszek Krček was a linguist who earned his doctorate from the University of Lviv and studied under Josef Zubatý at Charles University, Leipzig, and Berlin. In 1909, he served as a docent at the University of Lviv.

Franciszek Ksawery Malinowski was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the Major Seminary of Pelplin and the University of Warsaw (~1827–1831), becoming a member of the Polish Academy of Arts and Sciences in 1873.

Franciszek Machalski was a scholar of Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Lviv under Stefan Bołeslaw Stasiak, later working there (~1934–1939) and serving as professor at Jagiellonian University (1951–1974).

Franciszek Tokarz was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at the University of Lviv under Stefan Bołeslaw Stasiak and Jan Otrębski, and at Jagiellonian University under Helena Willman-Grabowska, later teaching Sanskrit at the Catholic University of Lublin (1954–1970).
